subject: Notion
a: Notion replaced your five apps with one app that does all five slightly worse and takes a small eternity to load.
b: Notion is where teams spend three hours building the perfect dashboard to avoid doing the work the dashboard tracks.

subject: Figma
a: Figma tried to sell itself to Adobe, regulators said no, and that was still the most exciting thing design tooling did all year.
b: Figma gives you an infinite canvas, infinite comments, and exactly one file nobody is allowed to touch before the meeting.

subject: Slack
a: Slack calls itself where work happens, which is true, if the work is being interrupted every ninety seconds by a thumbs up.
b: Slack turned the open-plan office into a website, so now you can be distracted from home too.

subject: Zoom
a: Hi, I built Zoom. My greatest innovation is a mute button that half the planet still cannot locate under pressure.
b: We are Zoom. We connected the world, then taught it the phrase you are on mute, which is now our real product.

subject: Cursor
a: Cursor lets you build a startup without learning to code, which explains the growing pile of startups nobody can debug.
b: Cursor is an editor that writes the bug, apologizes, writes a fresh bug, and calls the whole thing pair programming.

subject: Vercel
a: Hi, I am Vercel. We ship your site in seconds and rewrite the framework it depends on roughly as often.
b: We are Vercel. Deployment is instant. Working out which of our seven caching layers broke is the part that takes a week.

subject: Substack
a: Substack convinced every journalist to quit and become a small business owner who now emails you about their content calendar.
b: Substack is where you pay five dollars a month to feel guilty about not reading someone you used to follow for free.

subject: Humane AI Pin
a: Humane built a wearable that beams a menu onto your palm, and the market reviewed it straight back into the box.
b: The Humane Pin promised a phone-free future and mainly delivered a warm chest and a very active returns desk.

subject: Rabbit R1
a: Hi, I made the Rabbit R1. It is a bright orange gadget that does what your phone already does, only slower and easier to lose.
b: We are Rabbit. We reinvented the assistant as a small orange box, then discovered it was basically an app the whole time.

subject: WeWork
a: Hi, we are WeWork. We rented offices, added beanbags and the word community, and briefly convinced everyone that made us a tech company.
b: We are WeWork. Our breakthrough was leasing buildings long, renting them short, and calling the gap elevated consciousness.
